subject.title: Session Routing Bugs: CLI routing to wrong session, WeChat ID inconsistency, and session deadlock from message flooding

question: Should #88204 be split into focused core/plugin issues, and what canonical behavior should OpenClaw use for default TUI sessions, WeChat sessionId lineage repair, background event isolation, and meaningful activity ordering?
rationale: Current source shows partial fixes and multiple owner boundaries, but choosing dedicated TUI sessions, usage-family repair semantics, and WeChat plugin ownership is product direction rather than a safe automatic patch.

options.title: Split into focused issues
options.body: Track meaningful activity under #51028, open or reuse separate TUI and WeChat routing items, and require live proof for the WeChat/flood slices before implementation.

options.title: Sponsor one session-routing project
options.body: Keep #88204 as the umbrella and have an owner design the full activity, routing, and background-event model before coding.

options.title: Defer WeChat-specific repair to plugin owners
options.body: Keep only the generic core gaps in OpenClaw and route plugin-specific identity repair to @tencent-weixin/openclaw-weixin after live reproduction.

recommendation.title: Split into focused issues
recommendation.body: Track meaningful activity under #51028, open or reuse separate TUI and WeChat routing items, and require live proof for the WeChat/flood slices before implementation.

likelyOwner.reason: He is the strongest current-main routing signal across the TUI, session projection, store, and subagent steering surfaces that need splitting.
